land.text: Bithynia's first shape, which lies inside Cliopatria's Achaemenid outline of 337

predecessors.note: The pages opened say nothing of Persian rule or of its end in Bithynia; the handover is Cliopatria's overlap.

land.text: the whole kingdom, a Roman province from 74 BC ('The Senate immediately voted to annex the kingdom')

successors.note: The kingdom page's infobox date is 74 BC; Cliopatria draws it to 67.

capitals.name: Nicomedia (Izmit)
capitals.note: Infobox capital; founded 264 BC (Eusebius). The seat before 264 is not named on the pages opened.

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 14,644 km2 around Nicomedia and the Gulf of Izmit. The page says the kingdom 'seems to have been established in the 4th century BC' and that the native prince Bas 'managed to defeat Alexander the Great's general Calas in battle (probably around 330 BC)'; it gives no boundary, so the shape stands on Cliopatria alone.
The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 14,450 km2, the same core. Nothing on the page changes it between Alexander's conquests and the Diadochi.
The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 14,594 km2, the same core through the Wars of the Diadochi; the page does not mention Lysimachus, Antigonus or Zipoetes' wars (page silent).

The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 14,450 km2. The page dates Zipoetes' royal title to 297: 'assumed the Greek title of basileus (meaning king) in 297 BC'; the infobox gives 'Zipoetes I (first)' 297-278 BC. The outline does not change with the title.

The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 14,644 km2, the shape Nicomedes I inherited in 278 ('whom he succeeded on the throne in 278 BC'). Antiochus I 'did in fact invade Bithynia, but withdrew without risking battle'; 'no details are recorded, either of the war or of the peace which ended it'.

The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 27,393 km2: Cliopatria adds 11,900 km2 in 279, inland between 29.6E and 32.3E and 40.1N and 40.8N (the added cells all lie inside the Seleucid Empire's 280 outline). Neither the Kingdom of Bithynia nor the Nicomedes I page records a territorial gain ('The article does not describe any territorial gains or losses'), so the growth is the ledger's confidence-1 bridge. The same year Cliopatria first draws Galatia, Pergamon, Paphlagonia and Pontus around it.

The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 29,831 km2: +2,400 km2 (seven cells between 29.0E and 29.4E, 40.2N and 40.6N) around Cius (Gemlik) and Myrleia (Mudanya). 'Philip V granted him the cities of Kios and Myrleia in 202 BC': the shape starts a year before the grant, which is therefore a ledger event at the interval's edge. Byzantium's Asiatic territory (220: 'seizing its Asiatic territory') is already inside Cliopatria's 279 outline, so the 220 gain adds nothing to the picture. Cliopatria books the added cells to the Seleucid Empire's 204 outline, but the page names Philip V as the giver.

The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 29,903 km2, unchanged but for 72 km2. 'Becoming king in 127 BC, Nicomedes III conquered Paphlagonia along the Black Sea' (the Cliopatria Paphlagonia row ends in 127), but the Nicomedes III page says he partitioned it with Mithridates VI and that the senate 'ordered Nicomedes III to leave Paphlagonia' with no dates. The share is not drawn; the ledger carries it as an occupation (confidence 1).

correction.text: the shape unchanged for 91-89; Pontus occupies it in 90 and from early 88 until the treaty of Dardanos in 85

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 30,024 km2. The outline holds for 91-89 only: 'Mithridates VI defeated Nicomedes IV in 90 BC and annexed Bithynia' and Rome restored him the same year (Kingdom page, Mithridatic War page: 'restored the two kings without a fight', end of 90), then 'Mithridates rapidly exploited the void left by the Romans' departure and captured Bythinia without opposition' in early 88. The shape is unchanged; the Pontic occupations of 90 and 88-85 are ledger events, and Cliopatria draws no Bithynia for 87-78.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 77 shape, unchanged, standing for the whole kingdom of Nicomedes IV: under Pontic occupation in 87-85, restored by the treaty of Dardanos (late summer or early autumn 85)

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. New keyframe for Cliopatria's gap 87-78: the kingdom did not end in 88. Sulla's treaty of Dardanos (85) required Mithridates to 'restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia', Mithridates 'later reconciled with Nicomedes', and Bithynia 'stayed neutral during the Second Mithridatic War (83-81 BC)'. The 87-85 years are Pontic occupation (hatched); the page does not confirm the date of Nicomedes IV's actual return.

correction.text: the shape unchanged for 77-75; from 74 it is the Roman province of Bithynia

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. 30,213 km2. The shape is right for 77-75 only: 'In 74 BC, Nicomedes IV died and... bequeathed his kingdom to Rome' and 'The Senate immediately voted to annex the kingdom as a province directly governed by the Republic'; Cliopatria keeps the kingdom to 67. The land from 74 is the Roman province (roman-republic); Pontus' 73 reoccupation, the Third Mithridatic War, is not on the pages opened.

region.text: Bithynia around Nicomedia and the Gulf of Izmit, Cliopatria's first shape

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: the kingdom 'seems to have been established in the 4th century BC'; Cliopatria's first Bithynian shape is 333. The native prince Bas 'managed to defeat Alexander the Great's general Calas in battle (probably around 330 BC)'. Cliopatria's Achaemenid outline of 337 contains the whole shape (49 of its 50 cells).
297: Zipoetes takes the royal title. He 'assumed the Greek title of basileus (meaning king) in 297 BC'; infobox '297-278 BC: Zipoetes I (first)'. The dynasty of Bithynia becomes a kingdom.

region.text: the inland growth of Cliopatria's 279 outline over its 281 outline, 29.6E to 32.3E

ledger.note: Page silent: no page opened records a Bithynian gain in 279-278. Nicomedes I 'succeeded on the throne in 278 BC' after Antiochus I 'invade[d] Bithynia, but withdrew without risking battle'; Cliopatria's 279 outline adds 11,900 km2 taken from its Seleucid 280 outline. Bridging only.

264: Nicomedes I founds Nicomedia, the capital. 'The founding of Nicomedia is placed by Eusebius in 264 BC' near the Megarian colony of Astakos; the page does not say the court moved there and names no earlier seat.

region.text: the Asiatic territory of Byzantium on the Bosporus and its Chalcedon shore

ledger.note: 220: Prusias I takes Byzantium's Asian shore. He 'fought a war against Byzantium in 220 BC, seizing its Asiatic territory'; the page does not say where. The place is the researcher's reading (Chalcedon, Kadikoy).

region.text: Cius (Gemlik) and Myrleia (Mudanya) on the Propontis

ledger.note: 202: Philip V gives Prusias I Cius and Myrleia. 'Philip V granted him the cities of Kios and Myrleia in 202 BC'; he renamed them Prusias and Apameia. Cliopatria's 203 outline already holds them and books the cells to the Seleucid Empire.

127 or after: Nicomedes III takes Paphlagonia. 'Becoming king in 127 BC, Nicomedes III conquered Paphlagonia along the Black Sea.' The Nicomedes III page says Mithridates VI 'invaded Paphlagonia and drove its ruler... out' and that 'the two kings then partitioned it', undated; the year is set to the accession and to the end of Cliopatria's Paphlagonia row.

region.text: Paphlagonia, which the senate ordered Nicomedes III to leave

ledger.note: Page undated: 'the senate ordered Nicomedes III to leave Paphlagonia'; set at the end of his reign (c. 94 BC, infobox).

90: Mithridates VI drives out Nicomedes IV. 'Mithridates VI defeated Nicomedes IV in 90 BC and annexed Bithynia.' The Mithridatic War page: 'Mithridates took possession of Bithynia by expelling his nephew Nicomedes IV' (no precise year).

90: Rome restores Nicomedes IV. 'After having restored the two kings without a fight' (Nicomedes and Ariobarzanes), dated by the page to the end of 90 BC; the Kingdom page: 'Rome restored Nicomedes IV'.

88: Mithridates VI takes Bithynia again. 'Mithridates rapidly exploited the void left by the Romans' departure and captured Bythinia without opposition' (early 88); Nicomedes' army had been 'soundly defeated' at the Amnias in 89.

region.text: Bithynia, evacuated by Mithridates at the treaty of Dardanos

ledger.note: 85: the treaty of Dardanos. 'The final meeting took place at Dardanos on the Troad coast in late summer or early autumn 85'; Sulla demanded that Mithridates 'restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia, surrender all his conquests'. The page does not say when the troops left or whether the senate ratified (it 'was never ratified').

region.text: the whole kingdom, bequeathed to Rome

ledger.note: 74: Nicomedes IV bequeaths Bithynia to Rome. 'Nicomedes IV bequeathed the Kingdom of Bithynia to the Roman Republic: 74 BC' (infobox); 'The Senate immediately voted to annex the kingdom as a province directly governed by the Republic.'
74: the Kingdom of Bithynia ends. Nicomedes IV 'died and... bequeathed his kingdom to Rome'; the land becomes a Roman province. Cliopatria draws the kingdom to 67.

wars.name: Bas against Calas
wars.outcome: Bas 'managed to defeat Alexander the Great's general Calas in battle (probably around 330 BC)': Bithynia stays out of Alexander's empire.

wars.name: Antiochus I's invasion of Bithynia
wars.outcome: 'Antiochus did in fact invade Bithynia, but withdrew without risking battle'; 'no details are recorded, either of the war or of the peace which ended it'.
wars.note: The page dates neither the invasion nor the peace; the year is Cliopatria's 279 change and the war is listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

wars.name: Nicomedes I's war with Zipoetes II and the Galatian crossing
wars.outcome: Nicomedes killed two brothers, allied with Heraclea Pontica and Antigonus II Gonatas, brought the Celts 'engaged in the siege of Byzantium in 277 BC' across into Asia and turned them on Zipoetes II.
wars.note: The Celts settle in Cliopatria's Galatia row from 279; no Bithynian territory changes on the page.

wars.name: Prusias I's war with Byzantium
wars.outcome: Prusias I seized Byzantium's Asiatic territory in 220 BC.

wars.name: Prusias I's wars with Pergamon and Heraclea Pontica
wars.outcome: Prusias 'expanded the territories of Bithynia in a series of wars' against Attalus I of Pergamon and Heraclea Pontica; he took Cierus and renamed it Prusias, besieged Heraclea and lifted the siege when wounded; he made peace 'with presumably Eumenes II of Pergamon in 183 BC' at Cyzicus.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the wars; the span is his reign to the 183 peace. Cliopatria's Pergamon grows to 176,000 km2 in 188 (Treaty of Apamea) while Bithynia does not change.

wars.name: Prusias II's invasion of Pergamon
wars.outcome: The invasion failed in 154 BC and Bithynia had to pay war reparations.
wars.note: The page's sentence is ambiguous about whose ally Rome was; no territory changed.

wars.name: Nicomedes III and Mithridates VI in Paphlagonia
wars.outcome: Mithridates 'invaded Paphlagonia and drove its ruler... out' and the two kings partitioned it; the senate 'ordered Nicomedes III to leave Paphlagonia'.
wars.note: Neither the partition nor the senate's order is dated on the pages opened; the span is Nicomedes III's reign (c. 127-94).

wars.name: First Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Nicomedes IV beaten at the Amnias (89); Mithridates takes Asia 'through Phrygia' in early 88 and Bithynia 'without opposition'; the treaty of Dardanos (85) 'was in effect a return to the status quo of 89'.
wars.note: Mithridates VI had first expelled Nicomedes IV in 90 (Kingdom page).

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary line; Bithynia is described by its towns and neighbours, not borders. Every edge is approximate.

sources.title: Kingdom of Bithynia
sources.note: Infobox (Nicomedia, no area, 74 BC end), Zipoetes 297, Bas and Calas, Prusias II, Nicomedes III, the Mithridatic wars, the 74 BC bequest. Thin on territory.

sources.title: Nicomedes I of Bithynia
sources.note: Accession 278, Antiochus I's invasion, the Celts in 277, Nicomedia 264. No territorial gain recorded.

sources.title: Prusias I of Bithynia
sources.note: Byzantium 220, Cius and Myrleia 202, peace of 183, death 182.

sources.title: Nicomedes III of Bithynia
sources.note: Paphlagonia partitioned and the senate's order, both undated; reign c. 127-94.

sources.title: First Mithridatic War
sources.note: Restoration of 90, Amnias 89, the 88 conquest, Dardanos 85.

notes:
Pages opened: five (budget up to 5 for 10 shapes): Kingdom of Bithynia, Nicomedes I, Prusias I, Nicomedes III, First Mithridatic War. The kingdom page is thin on territory and gives no infobox area, so no keyframe has an area ratio; the Wikipedia infobox 'Area' field is empty.
Cliopatria problems: (1) the 279 growth (11,900 km2, drawn out of the Seleucid Empire's 280 shape) has no territorial sentence behind it on any page opened; the 203 growth (seven cells at Cius and Myrleia, also drawn out of the Seleucid 204 shape) is the 202 gift of Philip V of Macedon, who is not the Seleucids; the Byzantine Asiatic territory of 220 is already inside the 279 outline. (2) Cliopatria has no Bithynia for 87-78; the kingdom survived the Pontic occupation of 88-85 (Dardanos) and 'stayed neutral during the Second Mithridatic War (83-81 BC)': a new keyframe fills the gap. (3) The 77-67 shape runs seven years past 74, when Nicomedes IV bequeathed the kingdom to Rome. (4) The Paphlagonian conquest of Nicomedes III is not in any Cliopatria shape and is not dated on any page; it is carried as a hatched occupation 127-94 at confidence 1.
Not settled: the pre-297 history of the dynasty and its seat (the page names Nicomedia only; Nicaea, Astacus and Bithynion are not on the pages opened, so the capital list starts at 264); the extent of the territory gained at the Treaty of Apamea period and in the 183 peace; the Treaty of Apamea and the Seleucid shape in 189-188 (Cliopatria's allegiance row of Seleucid Empire to Rome); Heraclea Pontica and Cierus under Prusias I (no dates); Nicomedes II's reign (149-127) and Prusias II (182-149) beyond the 154 invasion; the Third Mithridatic War (73 BC onward), which sits with the Pontus and Roman Republic dossiers; the rulers list (the pages give only the first, last and a few reigns; no list of kings page was opened, so identity.rulers is omitted).
Counterparts: seleucid-empire, antigonid-macedonia, kingdom-of-pontus, roman-republic, paphlagonia (all with Cliopatria rows); Byzantium and Heraclea Pontica are not Cliopatria rows (Byzantium falls inside the Greek City-States row at most) and may need dossiers from eu-01. Region names used: Bithynia, Paphlagonia (regions.jsonl); Cius (Gemlik), Myrleia (Mudanya) and Chalcedon are given as coordinates because the gazetteer lacks them.
